paragraphs: Friend, here's the whole song in one breath: the LORD is David's shepherd, so David lacks nothing he needs. Everything else in Psalm 23 is David showing us what that looks like. Grass to rest in, quiet waters, a soul that gets restored, and a path to walk, all "for the sake of His name" (Psalm 23:1-3). FULL. SERVICE. SHEPHERD.

Then the road gets dark, and David doesn't pretend it doesn't. He walks through "the valley of the shadow of death," and he says, "I will fear no evil, for You are with me" (Psalm 23:4). Notice what changes his fear. The valley doesn't get shorter or easier. The shepherd is just right there, and the rod and staff comfort him. I think that's the most honest comfort there is, friend, because it works in the real valleys and not only the pretty meadows.

The picture flips at the end, and David is a guest at the LORD's table, even "in the presence of my enemies." His head is anointed with oil, and his cup overflows (Psalm 23:5). He closes by looking at ALL his days: "Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever" (Psalm 23:6). So the big idea is this: with the LORD as your shepherd, you're cared for in the pasture, kept in the valley, welcomed at the table, and brought all the way home.
